title: Morphisms out of a homotopically projective DG module in D(A,d)
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. For right differential graded $A$-modules $M,N$ let $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(M,N)$ be the complex whose degree-$r$ elements are families of additive maps $f:M^j\to N^{j+r}$ with $f(ma)=f(m)a$, with differential $df=d_Nf-(-1)^rfd_M$. Its closed degree-zero elements are the module maps commuting with the differentials, and two of them are chain homotopic when their difference is $dh$ for some $h$ of degree $-1$; thus the homotopy category $K(A,d)$ has $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A,d)}(M,N)=H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(M,N)$, and $D(A,d)$ is its localization, with localization functor $K(A,d)\to D(A,d)$. Call a right differential graded $A$-module $P$ homotopically projective if $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(P,N)$ is acyclic for every right differential graded $A$-module $N$ with $H^i(N)=0$ for all $i$. If $P$ is homotopically projective, then for every right differential graded $A$-module $N$ the map $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A,d)}(P,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(P,N)$ induced by the localization functor is bijective. No boundedness, freeness or countability assumption is imposed on $P$, $N$ or $A$; the cases $P=0$ and $N=0$ are included.

source.place: Tag 09KY, lemma-hom-derived, part (1) and its proof (the only input on P used there is the vanishing of Tag 09KM, lemma-property-P-K-projective, i.e. homotopical projectivity).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-dg-homotopy-acyclic-localization], $\mathcal T=K(A,d)$ is triangulated, its strictly full subcategory $\mathcal E$ of acyclic DG modules is triangulated, and the morphisms with a cone in $\mathcal E$ are exactly the quasi-isomorphisms. Consequently the functor $L:K(A,d)\to D(A,d)$ specified in the statement is a localization at precisely $W_{\mathcal E}$. This checks the categorical hypotheses of the general orthogonal localization theorem; the ambient category is the DG-module homotopy category, rather than the homotopy category of ordinary complexes of modules over the underlying graded ring.

For every $E\in\mathcal E$, homotopical projectivity makes $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(P,E)$ acyclic. Its zeroth cohomology is therefore zero. The identity $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A,d)}(P,E)=H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(P,E)$ in the statement now gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A,d)}(P,E)=0$: every closed degree-zero map is a boundary, hence is null homotopic. Thus $P$ is left orthogonal to $\mathcal E$. No property-(P) resolution or termwise projectivity is used. All shifts of acyclic modules already belong to $\mathcal E$, so this also supplies the shifted vanishing used in the source proof.

source.place: Tag 09KY, lemma-hom-derived, proof of (1), the vanishing input attributed there to Tag 09KM; here it follows directly from the stronger Hom-complex hypothesis in the item.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-left-orthogonal-localization-hom] with $\mathcal T=K(A,d)$, the subcategory $\mathcal E$ of step 1, the object $P$ of step 2, and $L$ the stated localization. For every DG module $N$ it gives the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A,d)}(P,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(LP,LN)$, and its statement identifies this map as $f\mapsto L(f)$. This is exactly the required canonical map. The two inputs impose no bounds on degrees or cardinality, and their hypotheses still hold when $P=0$, $N=0$ or $A$ is the zero ring.
